**Finding submitted: deviation (WARRANTY).**

- **What the document does:** Subparagraph 4.9 (p0126–p0127) is a pure disclaimer — the PG makes no representations or warranties as to Supplier performance, Wet Segment performance/reliability, or integration into operation, and closes with a catch-all that nothing in the Agreement may be construed as a warranty. Searches for "warrant", conformance-to-specification, defect/repair/replace/refund language turned up no express warranty anywhere; Subparagraph 4.8 (p0124–p0125) only gives the PG a discretionary right to pursue Supply Contract remedies, subject to Management Committee direction, which is not a remedy running to us. Paragraph 10 maintenance duties ("efficient working order") are covenants, not a conformance warranty.
- **Classification:** effectively "as is" with all warranties disclaimed — walk-away territory, so the fallback fails on a material term.
- **Cure (fallback target, three surgical ops):** insert a new Subparagraph 4.10 carrying only the four fallback elements (90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, repair or replacement, refund of fees paid), and add a narrow "except as expressly provided in Subparagraph 4.10" carve-out to both limbs of the 4.9 disclaimer so no retained words contradict the new warranty. All untouched wording is preserved verbatim; the minimality gate returned ok:true.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the preferred position's compliance-with-laws element is already satisfied by Paragraph 25, and we did not upgrade to 12-month/professional-and-workmanlike/no-malicious-code wording since fallback is the shortest complete cure.
